observation: Measured in a local Chromium against the built 2.0 homepage on 2026-09-09: white text on the brand blue #0090CC primary button reaches 3.58:1; route-card link text in #0090CC on white reaches 3.58:1; the section eyebrow in #0090CC on #f4f6f8 reaches 3.31:1; body and card text in #76777A on white reaches 4.48:1. WCAG 2.1 AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. The hero rotating line in #0090CC at 38.4px and 600 weight reaches 3.58:1 and therefore passes as large text.
evidence_locator: OM Website Skill Suite v1.2.0 canon.json visual_tokens, contrast_status not_tested
why_it_matters: The primary button is the one control the whole homepage drives toward, and its label is the least readable text on the page. The canon records contrast_status as not_tested, so this is the first measurement rather than a regression.
competing_explanation: The palette was chosen for brand recognition from the OM social graphics reference, not for text contrast, and #0090CC does pass as large display type. It is legitimate to keep it wherever it appears large. The failure is specific to small text and to white-on-blue controls, not to the colour itself.
proposed_change: Keep #0090CC as the brand fill, border, stripe and large-display colour, including the hero rotating line, which passes unchanged. Introduce one darker token of the same hue for small text and for control backgrounds: --blue-ink #007CB2, which reaches 4.64:1 against white and carries white text at 4.64:1. Apply it to .btn-blue background, .route-card a, .kicker and any blue text below 18.66px. Darken --gray from #76777A to #747578, which reaches 4.61:1 and is visually indistinguishable at text sizes.
alternatives_considered: Navy #243746 text on a #0090CC button reaches only 3.43:1 and also fails.
Darkening the single --blue token sitewide would change the hero line and every brand fill, which is a larger visual change than the failure requires.
smallest_useful_test: Apply the two token changes in a local preview, then re-measure the four failing pairs and confirm each reaches 4.5:1 or better, that the hero line and brand fills are unchanged, and that no dark-section pair regresses below its current ratio.
decision_criterion: All four failing pairs reach 4.5:1 or better; #0090CC still appears as the hero rotating line, card top borders and brand fills; no previously passing pair drops.
approval_note: Protected visual tokens are sourced to S-VISUAL. Under the improvement protocol an M2 change is proposed only until the responsible person approves the exact values. The change is staged and not applied.
rollback: Revert the two custom-property values in styles.css. No markup or copy changes are involved.
